links.comparator_used: Baseline frontier LLM without retrieval (Model A)
links.outcome: Clinical reasoning score across nine cognitive steps in longitudinal nephrology cases
links.effect: Human evaluation (20-point scale): Model B 16.2 (SD 1.2) vs Model A 16.1 (SD 1.3), no significant improvement. AI panel (15-point scale): Model B 14.3 vs Model A 14.2.
links.quote: Implementing static RAG (Model B) yielded no significant improvement over the baseline.

links.comparator_used: Single baseline frontier LLM (Model A) and LLM with static guideline RAG (Model B)
links.outcome: Overall clinical reasoning score, diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic management scores
links.effect: Human evaluation (20-point scale): Model C 17.2 (SD 1.2) vs Model A 16.1 and Model B 16.2 (P < 0.001). AI panel (15-point scale): Model C 14.7 vs Model A 14.2 (P < 0.001) and Model B 14.3 (P = 0.01). Diagnostic accuracy 17.6 (P = 0.019); therapeutic management 17.3 (P = 0.002).
links.quote: Distributing clinical workflows into a multi-agent dynamic refinement pipeline significantly improves reasoning completeness, intercepts error cascades, and safely resolves planning bottlenecks in complex patient care.

links.comparator_used: LLM with static guideline-based RAG and no iterative self-critique (Model B)
links.outcome: Clinical reasoning score in longitudinal nephrology cases
links.effect: Human evaluation (20-point scale): Model C (RAG plus iterative self-critique and refinement) 17.2 vs Model B 16.2 (P < 0.001). AI panel: 14.7 vs 14.3 (P = 0.01). Model C was also a multi-agent framework, so the self-critique effect is confounded with the agent decomposition.
links.quote: Static knowledge retrieval alone fails to enhance frontier LLM performance in longitudinal medical reasoning.

design_hint: retrieval grounding and iterative self-critique refinement added to baseline LLM
